text:
UTA arrives in Ottawa after a bruising 5-4 overtime loss at MTL, where the Canadiens erased a two-goal deficit despite a Logan Cooley hat trick. The Mammoth are 2-2-1 in their last five and are without John Marino, with Andrew Peeke moving in beside Schmidt and Mikhail Sergachev now playing 25:40 a night. OTT is also 2-2-1 in its last five, fresh off a 2-1 win at BUF, but is missing William Eklund, Ridly Greig and Andre Burakovsky. Tim Stützle has taken Eklund's spot beside Cozens and Zetterlund.

UTA has controlled more of the play, taking 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five to OTT's 52%. OTT's penalty kill allows 0.87 expected goals a game against a UTA power play that creates 0.83, and OTT takes 4.9 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays. In net, projected starter Karel Vejmelka sits at -6.8 goals saved above expected this season (after +5.4 last year), and projected OTT starter Samuel Ersson is at -0.9 (after -17.8). Neither goalie is giving his team much cover.

Cooley is the name to watch for UTA, with a 34% chance to score and 15 points in his last 10 games. He was drafted third overall in 2022, one pick after Simon Nemec. For OTT, Stützle has the best odds on either side at 35% to score and 76% to record a point, and Drake Batherson is right behind at 32%. Our model sees this as close to even, at 3.21 expected goals for UTA and 3.13 for OTT.
